# Independent audit of ordinary depth Brunn--Minkowski rigidity

Audited `candidate 6c56e9569b9982d7`
in full. **PASS; no mathematical correction needed.** The proof is
ordinary continuous geometry and does not substitute a mixed-fiber
section formula.

At an interior candidate every through-point section is proper and
has positive relative volume. After rotation, vertical intervals
give the asserted angular derivative by Fubini. Relative interior
points of the section are interior to the body, so their vertical
intervals contain zero in their interiors. Off the section the
pointwise derivative is zero; its relative boundary is null. The
difference quotient is bounded by the indicated linear function
on a bounded projection. Thus dominated convergence applies even
for polytopes and all nonsmooth full bodies. Vanishing derivatives
in every tangent direction force the section centroid to be the
candidate itself.

The positive-balance proof at a deepest point has the correct
movement sign. Separating active normals have positive dot product
with v; moving the point in direction minus v adds a uniformly
positive own-body slab to nearby active directions. The compact
inactive set retains a positive gap. An interior ball and a bounded
outer ball supply the required uniform lower and upper slab
bounds. The selected finitely many positively balanced normals
give a closed whole-space cap cover regardless of their rank.

Under equality of the A-root Brunn--Minkowski inequality, each
selected active cap of the Minkowski sum forces equality at every
step of its endpoint cap-volume chain. Strict positivity of both
coefficients is essential and correctly stated. The two endpoint
caps therefore attain their own ordinary minima and are positively
homothetic with the same volume-determined ratio in every selected
direction. Their minimum exposed faces are the actual proper
through-center sections. The preceding section-centroid identity
forces every homothety translation to equal g_L minus r g_K.
The balanced cap cover then covers both entire bodies by these
aligned pieces, so global homothety follows. This closes the
potential gap of allowing unrelated deformations outside one cap.

Strict inclusion monotonicity follows correctly by sandwiching
the midpoint between the nested bodies, invoking the equality
classification, and then using strict ordinary volume increase
under proper full-dimensional convex inclusion. No uniform gap
is claimed.

For strict pointwise quasiconcavity, unequal endpoint thresholds
would make the larger-threshold endpoint cap strictly smaller than
the intermediate cap: all intervening levels are proper and have
positive section area. Equal thresholds would make the same plane
active at both endpoint candidates. Its unique section centroid
cannot equal two distinct points. This proves strictness, including
unequal endpoint depth values. Continuity then supplies the stated
strictly convex positive submaximal depth regions and the unique
deepest point. The d=1 singleton-section convention is consistent
throughout.

Finally, zero A-root surplus at an actual compatible midpoint
first gives equality of A with the Minkowski midpoint, then equality
of the actual bodies by strict inclusion, and finally homothety by
the proved Brunn--Minkowski equality theorem. This conclusion is
only for the tested relation. It does not imply untested Jensen
relations from a forest, and the note explicitly preserves that
distinction.
